paper_metadata.title: Processing, microstructure evolution and mechanical property improvements of an Al–V–Cr–Mn–Fe–Ni CCA with an as-cast BCC/B2 coherent nanostructure

evidence.quote: an Al–V–Cr–Mn–Fe–Ni complex concentrated alloy (CCA) with an as-cast microstructure consisting of coherent B2 precipitation in a BCC matrix
a thermo-mechanical processing route ... was developed using an Al–V–Cr–Mn–Fe–Ni CCA
the same method was applied to an Al–Cr–Fe–Co–Ni CCA composition found in the literature
subsequently validated using an Al–Cr–Fe–Co–Ni CCA found in literature
Ingots with a nominal composition of Al9.64V4.32Cr10.94Mn12.98-Fe44.12Ni18 (at. %) were produced by arc-melting of raw elements with purities over 99.9% (wt. %) under a Ti-gettered argon atmosphere.
Both Al9.64V4.32Cr10.94Mn12.98Fe44.12Ni18 and Al12.5Cr17.5Fe35-Co17.5Ni17.5 showed significant improvements in their tensile performance after processing.
Fig. 2 shows the microstructure characterization and cold-rolling behavior of Al9.64V4.32Cr10.94Mn12.98Fe44.12Ni18 after the above-mentioned softening treatment.
The specimen for comparing with the as-cast specimen were annealed at 1265 ◦C in order to achieve the same fractions of BCC and FCC phases.
As shown in Figs. 4 and 5, the 1280 ◦C-annealed (1280C) sample has an equiaxed BCC grain structure, with no FCC phase on the grain boundaries nor inside the grains.
As the annealing temperature lowered to 1200 ◦C, some FCC crystals formed on the grain boundaries (around 20% in fraction measured by EBSD) can be observed.
With another drop of the annealing temperature to 1150 ◦C, the fraction of FCC phase further increased and nearly all the grain boundaries were decorated by FCC crystals (~31%)

As the annealing temperature lowered to 1100 ◦C, the second phase change in the microstructure occurred, where a coarser secondary B2 phase (several hundreds of nanometers in size) precipitated at the grain boundaries.
When the annealing temperature dropped to 1000 ◦C, both the size and fraction of the primary B2 precipitates have noticeably decreased

The third phase change occurred at the annealing temperature of 900 ◦C, where the primary fine coherent B2 precipitation in the BCC grains completely disappeared, leaving only the secondary coarse grain boundary B2 precipitates.
with the annealing temperature further lowered to 850 ◦C, the generally considered ‘detrimental sigma phase’ formed by replacing some of the previous BCC regions

Ingots with a nominal composition of Al9.64V4.32Cr10.94Mn12.98-Fe44.12Ni18 (at. %) were produced by arc-melting of raw elements with purities over 99.9% (wt. %) under a Ti-gettered argon atmosphere. Each ingot was flipped and remelted for at least 5 times to ensure chemical homogeneity.

other.purpose: phase transformation from BCC/B2 as-cast structure to FCC-dominant structure

evidence.quote: The alloyed ingots were softening-treated by annealing at 920 ◦C for 18 h. This process enables the phase transformation from the hard and brittle BCC/B2 as-cast structure to a soft and ductile FCC-dominant structure to gain the required ductility for heavy cold-working.
The softening treatment temperature for this composition was determined to be 1100 ◦C.
